A.explanation: Both forces $F$ are tangential with perpendicular distance $r$ from X and both tend to turn the disc the same way, so total moment is $Fr + Fr = 2Fr$.

B.explanation: Only one tangential force $F$ acts at distance $r$ from X, so the moment magnitude is $Fr$, not $2Fr$.

C.explanation: The two parallel forces $F$ act on opposite sides but in the same linear direction, so their $Fr$ moments about X oppose and cancel to zero.

D.explanation: The three forces $F$ do not all add in the same rotational sense about X, so the resultant moment magnitude is not $2Fr$.

hints: Notice whether each force $F$ at the disc edge is tangential or not, because only the perpendicular distance from X counts and this is $r$ for a tangent.
For each tangential force, decide clockwise or anticlockwise turning about X using $moment = Fr$ and check if the moments add or cancel.
Count how many $Fr$ contributions act in the same rotational sense to see which diagram can total $2Fr$ about X.
walkthrough: Moment about X is $force \times perpendicular$ $distance$ from X to the line of action of the force.
A force applied at the edge and tangent to the circular disc of radius $r$ has perpendicular distance $r$, so its moment magnitude is $F \times r = Fr$.
In arrangement A there are two such tangential forces: left side $F$ upward and right side $F$ downward.
Both tend to rotate the disc clockwise about X, so the moments have the same sign and add: $Fr + Fr = 2Fr$.
By contrast, B gives only $Fr$, C gives $Fr - Fr = 0$ because the turns oppose, and D does not give two full $Fr$ additions in the same sense.
Therefore the $2Fr$ moment about X is given by arrangement A. This is option A.
